help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The tall man reads. I see the tall man. I help the tall man.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The fresh bread is from the old bakery.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: den already shows masculine accusative, so the adjective takes the weak -en.
help.tips[0].en.text: Nom: der große / die große / das große / die großen. Akk: den großen / die große / das große / die großen. Dat: dem großen / der großen / dem großen / den großen. Gen: des großen / der großen / des großen / der großen.
help.tips[0].en.title: -e in five slots, -en everywhere else
help.tips[0].en.trap: the article did the work, so the adjective goes quiet. If the article shows the case clearly (den, dem, des, der-dative), the adjective is -en.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Feminine accusative sits in the little -e block, just like the nominative die neue Lehrerin.
help.tips[1].en.text: Picture the 4×4 table. Nominative row: e e e en. Accusative row: en e e en. Everything below: en. The -e's sit together in the top-left like a small window; the rest of the wall is -en.
help.tips[1].en.title: The little -e block
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The yellow flowers are on the table. I water the yellow flowers.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: I get on well with the new colleagues.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: After the plural die the adjective always ends in -en.
help.tips[2].en.text: die kleinen Kinder, die roten Schuhe, den kleinen Kindern, der roten Schuhe. No exceptions after a definite article.
help.tips[2].en.title: Plural is always -en after die
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Which old film do you mean? I know this little dog.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: Every new member of staff gets this little handbook.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: dieses shows neuter just like das, so the adjective takes the weak -e: das blaue Kleid, dieses blaue Kleid.
help.tips[3].en.text: dieser große Mann, jede junge Frau, welches neue Auto — the same two endings apply because these words show the case like der does.
help.tips[3].en.title: dieser, jeder, welcher, jener behave like der
help.context.en: The new colleague sits in the small office next to the big kitchen. Today I introduced the new colleague to the old boss. The colour of the new office is green, and the big windows look onto the beautiful park. At the end of the long day we drink together the strong coffee from the old machine.
help.hookEn: After der, die or das the adjective needs only two endings, -e or -en; learn which slot takes which and describe anything correctly.
help.introEn: This is the first table of the full adjective-ending system, and the easiest: after der, die, das (and dieser, jeder, welcher) the article already shows gender, number and case, so the adjective only needs a weak ending, and there are just two: -e or -en. -e in the five 'nominative-looking' slots — der große Mann, die junge Frau, das neue Auto (nominative), and die junge Frau, das neue Auto again (accusative feminine/neuter). -en everywhere else: den großen Mann, dem kleinen Kind, der netten Frau, des alten Hauses, and every plural (die roten Schuhe → den roten Schuhen). Draw the table once: the -e slots form a small block in the top left, the rest is -en. Any e-mail or description you write needs these endings right in simple phrases; this quiz drills them across all four cases.
help.recallEn.known: From "Adjektive vor dem Nomen: erste Begegnung": after der the adjective takes -e or -en.
help.recallEn.today: The full table, all four cases: -e in five cells, -en in all the others.
sentences[0].whyEn: After der/die/das only -e or -en. Nominative singular takes -e: der große Mann.
sentences[1].whyEn: Accusative masculine is the singular's exception: -en — den großen Mann.
sentences[2].whyEn: Nominative singular after die: -e — die junge Frau.
sentences[3].whyEn: Nominative singular after das: -e — das neue Auto.
sentences[4].whyEn: In the plural the ending after the article is always -en: die roten Schuhe.
sentences[5].whyEn: In the dative always -en: dem kleinen Kind.
sentences[6].whyEn: Plural after die: -en — die gelben Blumen.
sentences[8].whyEn: das-words don't change in the accusative: -e again — das frische Brot.
sentences[9].whyEn: Feminine stays the same in the accusative: -e — die alte Stadt.
sentences[10].whyEn: mit takes the dative, and the dative always takes -en: der netten Frau.
sentences[11].whyEn: Accusative neuter equals the nominative: -e — das große Haus.
sentences[13].whyEn: in + position = dative, so -en: in der langen Straße.
sentences[15].whyEn: dies- works like der: accusative masculine → -en — diesen berühmten Schauspieler.
sentences[16].whyEn: jed- counts like der; mit → dative → -en: jedem neuen Kollegen.
sentences[18].whyEn: Dative after diesem: -en — diesem alten Haus.
